# HTML diagrams: self-contained, accessible visual models (topology, sequence, state, hierarchy…)

Curated by Skill Harbor — @plannotator's html-diagram: a direct-invocation specialist for self-contained HTML diagrams whose layout, notation and interaction clarify a relationship better than prose. It picks the right model for the question (topology, sequence, process, state, hierarchy, timeline, matrix, quantitative), the right rendering method (HTML/CSS, SVG, Canvas, WebGL — never SVG-by-default), then delivers one dependency-free HTML file with inline CSS/JS, keyboard-accessible controls, prefers-reduced-motion support, and verification at wide and narrow widths (label collisions, clipped nodes, edge routing). MIT-licensed. Honest notes: it does not activate from general requests — the user must invoke it explicitly (or the parent html skill routes here); and it returns the absolute path plus what it simplified, so expect a deliverable, not a conversation. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
